about: Why each CRD test that did not pass did not pass. Rules are matched in order against the test id (and the message when given); the first match wins.

failures.cause: The coverage information update test reads the proposed Appointment targets, which the granted scopes test forbids Clear to grant. The two tests cannot both pass.
CapabilityStatement.instantiates is optional in US Core, and the HAPI server behind Clear's FHIR API cannot set it.
MedicationRequest search by patient, intent and authoredOn: the kit found no order values in the resources returned. Clear side, not yet analysed.
The US Core kit raises a NameError when Clear's FHIR API answers the Provenance revinclude search with HTTP 400 (the 400 itself is Clear's).

Probable cause: the kit checks the JWT exp when the test runs, several minutes after the hook request, not when the request arrived. The validator messages are not kept in results.json; to be confirmed on the next run.
Hook request content (granted scopes, prefetch profiles, stored coverage information). Clear side, not yet analysed.
Clear's read only FHIR API for the payer refused or rejected a US Core search (HTTP 400, 403 or 405). The run was before the later commits on the same branch.
US Core FHIR API check (capability statement, profile support, references, data absent reason). Clear side, not yet analysed.

notRun.reason: By design. The payer may read shared Practitioner, Organization, Location and Endpoint records only when the hook request names them (MetaCare decision, 2026-11-15), so the kit cannot resolve every must support reference.
US Core 3.1.1 and 6.1.0 FHIR API groups. The run tested Clear's FHIR API at US Core 7.0.0 only.
Scenario groups (long running hook, unknown content, self pay, multiple payers, user access level). Not run yet.
Cross hook groups. Not run yet.
US Core 7.0.0 tests skipped or not run because the synthetic record has no data of that kind, or an earlier search failed.
Visual inspection and attestation group. A person completes it in the Inferno interface; the run script does not.
